name_note: Eshraghiella was proposed for Butyrivibrio crossotus, which is why many genomes placed here carry the NCBI deposit name Butyrivibrio.

sentences.text: Eshraghiella was proposed within the family Lachnospiraceae when Butyrivibrio crossotus was reclassified as Eshraghiella crossota.
The reclassification rested on differences in 16S rRNA, groEL, recA and rpoB genes and in genome sequences that distinguish it from other Butyrivibrio species.
Comparative analysis reported digital DNA-DNA hybridization values of 19.40-27.20% and ANIb values of 67.06-67.64% against other Butyrivibrio species, below the species delineation thresholds.
Eshraghiella crossota was reported among species whose faecal relative abundance rose in Spanish participants over 62 after a three-month precision nutrition intervention.

references.title: Reclassification of Butyrivibrio crossotus Moore et al . 1976 (Approved Lists 1980) into a novel genus as Eshraghiella crossota gen. nov., comb. nov
